column1: # sub_82283480 -- where the flight model's three rate limits come from.
# Cycle 1376 left [model+1248/1252/1256] as "per-aircraft limits, source
# unknown". They have FOUR writers, and only one of them is a lookup:
#   0x82282220  the base constructor -- defaults, three image words
#   0x82283480  a speed-interpolated table lookup   <- this file
#   0x822F2520  writes +1256 only
#   0x82303D18  slot 9 of the sibling vtable 0x8200F310, writes all three
# THE DEFAULTS, read from the image rather than inferred:
# and immediately after them the base ctor writes 2000.0, 1800.0, 600.0, 200.0
# and 150.0 into nearby fields (0x82069E68, 0x82008B04, 0x82069EB8, 0x82069E40,
# 0x8200603C). Those are the magnitudes of aircraft speeds in km/h, which is the
# unit cycle 1374 established from the 9.8/3.6 and 1/3.6 pair.
# THE LOOKUP. sub_82283480 takes the model in r3 and a speed in f1, and:
#   1. searches a TEN-entry breakpoint table at [model+1076 .. +1112] for the
#      bracket containing |f1| (0x82283488..0x822834C8);
#   2. builds the interpolation weight 1/(hi-lo), guarded to 1.0 when the
#      bracket is degenerate (0x82283518);
#   3. interpolates between two SIXTEEN-BYTE records at [model+608 + index*16];
#   4. scales the three limits by three image constants and stores them back.
# THE THREE SCALES, resolved:
#                                                 uses for its own axis
# THE FOOTPRINT, measured by capsule and not by reading: seeding the model with
# a per-offset pattern and a monotone breakpoint table, then running it, changes
# exactly nine words.
